definitions.rationale: This is the macro equation expanding the fresh proof term madBody into the translated statement sequence, so it is a definitional abbreviation rather than an execution rule or additional theorem.
definitions.text:
rule madBody
    => Assign(Name("count"), Call(Name("len"), Name("numbers")))
       If(Compare(Name("count"), CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
          Return(Float(0.0)),
          .Stmts)
       Assign(Name("total"), Float(0.0))
       Assign(Name("number"), Float(0.0))
       For(Name("number"), Name("numbers"),
           Assign(Name("total"),
                  BinOp("+", Name("total"), Name("number"))))
       Assign(Name("mean"), BinOp("/", Name("total"), Name("count")))
       Assign(Name("deviation"), Float(0.0))
       For(Name("number"), Name("numbers"),
           Assign(Name("deviation"),
                  BinOp("+",
                        Name("deviation"),
                        Call(Name("abs"),
                             BinOp("-", Name("number"), Name("mean"))))))
       Return(BinOp("/", Name("deviation"), Name("count")))

definitions.rationale: This is the empty-sequence base equation for the newly defined recursive domain predicate allFloatVS.
This is the cons recurrence for the newly defined allFloatVS predicate and structurally descends on the sequence tail.
definitions.text:
rule allFloatVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq))
    => isFloat(V) andBool allFloatVS(R)

definitions.rationale: This guarded equation defines the fresh total proof symbol projectFloat in terms of the existing partial cast on the domain where that cast is defined.
definitions.text:
rule projectFloat(V:Val) => {V}:>Float
    requires isFloat(V)
    [concrete, simplification(10), preserves-definedness]

definitions.rationale: This is the reverse normalization orientation of the same guarded defining equation for the fresh projectFloat proof symbol, making the cast canonicalize to that named term.
definitions.text:
rule {V:Val}:>Float => projectFloat(V)
    requires isFloat(V)
    [symbolic(V), simplification, preserves-definedness]

definitions.rationale: This simplification equation gives projectFloat its identity case on values already of sort Float and therefore defines the fresh projection helper.
This is the empty-sequence base equation defining the fresh left-fold summary sumFloatVS.
This is the structurally recursive cons equation defining sumFloatVS by one addF step followed by the tail fold.
definitions.text:
rule sumFloatVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:Float)
    => sumFloatVS(R, addF(A, projectFloat(V)))

definitions.rationale: This is the empty-sequence base equation defining the fresh deviationFloatVS fold summary.
This is the structurally recursive cons equation defining deviationFloatVS through subtraction, absolute value, addition, and the tail fold.
definitions.text:
rule deviationFloatVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), M:Float, A:Float)
    => deviationFloatVS(
         R,
         M,
         addF(A, absF(subF(projectFloat(V), M))))

definitions.rationale: This guarded equation defines the zero-length branch of the fresh result summary madResult.
This complementary guarded equation defines the nonzero-length branch of madResult using the two fold summaries and the supplied division term.
definitions.text:
rule madResult(VS:ValSeq)
    => divFloatIntV(
         deviationFloatVS(
           VS,
           divFloatIntV(
             sumFloatVS(VS, 0.0),
             vsLen(VS)),
           0.0),
         vsLen(VS))
    requires vsLen(VS) =/=Int 0

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule asserts a definedness characterization for the pre-existing partial Val-to-Float cast; it is an additional mathematical fact, and Stage 1 does not first prove its exact statement in a module omitting the rule.

This simplification rule adds a guarded equality for the pre-existing applyBin operation at the dynamic Val sort; it is not a definition of a fresh symbol, and prove.sh does not establish the exact equality before compiling it.
source_rules.text:
rule applyBin("+", A:Float, V:Val)
    => addF(A, projectFloat(V))
    requires isFloat(V)
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule adds the analogous guarded subtraction equality for the pre-existing applyBin operation, and no rule-free Stage 1 proof first establishes its exact statement.
source_rules.text:
rule applyBin("-", V:Val, M:Float)
    => subF(projectFloat(V), M)
    requires isFloat(V)
    [simplification]
